title: [Roguelite] What Claude is good (or bad) at 👀
author: Groowl
selftext:
Shuriken Slam Jam is a one-button roguelite made with Claude and I'm happy to share with you some of my learnings.  
  
How the game works: you throw shurikens at your enemies, clear the rooms in a dungeon as quickly as possible, and collect incredibly powerful upgrades between each room.  


https://i.redd.it/baf66pvb4swh1.gif

  


**What Claude was actually good at:**  
  
0. **Coding fast** (lol)

1. **A balancing bench instead of gut feeling.** The game loads into a Node vm, and a bot plays real runs on the real game code, one run per CPU core. I give it a list of builds and it reports how far each one goes. When I change a number, I rerun the bench. Every balance change goes into the patch notes as before → after.  
  
2. **Art without image files.** Every sprite is drawn in code at runtime, so there isn’t a single image file in the game. Changing a color or the size of an enemy is one line, not a trip to an art tool.

**3. Procedural audio instead of assets.** The soundtrack is drum'n'bass synthesized live, and each upgrade you hold adds its own part. No licensing, and the music follows your build.  
  
**4. Scripted marketing.** The GIF you can see on this post but also Tiktok & Instagram contents come from a capture tool that plays the real game with chosen upgrades and records 60 fps clips.

**What AI was (really) bad at:** game feel & creative game mechanics. It can't tell you a throw feels mushy or a boss is boring. That part is still hours of playtesting.

Happy to answer questions about the workflow.

Free demo on itch io (playable on web browser or mobile) : [https://groowl.itch.io/shuriken-slam-jam-demo](https://groowl.itch.io/shuriken-slam-jam-demo)
